title: SemiAnalysis Tokenomics Model
gist: SemiAnalysis is marketing its AI Tokenomics Model as the first demand-side model of AI, linking token consumption and AI application revenue back to hardware demand for Nvidia GPUs, AMD GPUs, Google TPUs and Amazon Trainium, and to ROIC on hyperscaler, foundation-lab and neocloud deployments. Despite a URL implying an 'August tokenomics update', the captured text is a product/methodology description rather than an analytical update, so the signal here is framework structure and the implied worldview, not fresh data.

insights.claim: SemiAnalysis argues the AI research industry has lacked a demand-side model, and positions its AI Tokenomics Model as the first framework translating AI service revenue and usage growth into future hardware demand for Nvidia GPUs, AMD GPUs, Google TPUs and Amazon Trainium.
insights.speaker: SemiAnalysis
insights.so_what: If accelerator demand is now forecast from token consumption rather than capex announcements, inflections in application-layer usage become a leading indicator for semiconductor orders.
insights.quote: The Tokenomics model is the first demand-side model of AI that will allow users to translate revenue and usage growth into future AI hardware demand for Nvidia GPUs, AMD GPUs, Google TPUs, Amazon Trainium and more.
insights.locator: The SemiAnalysis AI Tokenomics Model connects

insights.claim: The central unresolved question SemiAnalysis frames for the AI buildout is the ROI and profitability of AI business models, which it explicitly labels a multi-trillion dollar question.
insights.speaker: SemiAnalysis
insights.so_what: Framing the debate around ROI rather than capacity implies the next derating risk for AI-levered equities comes from profitability disclosure, not supply constraints.
insights.quote: the multi-trillion dollar question: What is the ROI and profitability of AI business models?
insights.locator: Investors, corporates, policy makers and others

insights.claim: SemiAnalysis models ROIC on AI deployments separately for hyperscalers (Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Meta, Oracle), foundation labs (OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek) and neoclouds (CoreWeave, Nebius, Crusoe), implying the three cohorts earn structurally different returns on the same silicon.
insights.speaker: SemiAnalysis
insights.so_what: Segmenting AI returns by cohort is the setup for a dispersion trade: long the tier earning above cost of capital, short the tier renting depreciating assets at thin spreads.

themes.theme: Token throughput as the unit of account

insights.claim: SemiAnalysis builds bottoms-up token throughput forecasts from three stacked variables — hardware system, model architecture, and user workload — treating tokens per dollar as an output of that interaction rather than a fixed chip spec.
insights.speaker: SemiAnalysis
insights.so_what: Cost-per-token curves, not FLOPS, determine inference margins; watch model-architecture releases as much as hardware launches when sizing compute demand.
insights.quote: Bottoms-up token throughput forecasts taking into account

insights.claim: The workload mix modeled — coding, chat, document analysis and agentic use — is treated as a first-order driver of token demand, implying agentic workloads consume materially different token volumes per user than chat.
insights.speaker: SemiAnalysis
insights.so_what: A shift in usage mix toward agentic and coding workloads would raise inference demand far faster than user-count growth suggests.
insights.quote: User behavior/workloads (coding, chat, document analysis, agentic)

insights.claim: SemiAnalysis tracks named next-generation systems including GB200 NVL72, VR144, CPX, TPU v7 and Trainium 3 alongside models GPT-5, Sonnet 4, DeepSeek V3 and Kimi K2 as the concrete inputs to its throughput math.
insights.speaker: SemiAnalysis
insights.so_what: The named roadmap parts signal which accelerator generations SemiAnalysis expects to carry inference volume, a checklist for supply-chain and HBM order tracking.
insights.quote: Hardware system (GB200 NVL72, VR144, CPX, TPU v7, Trainium 3)

insights.claim: SemiAnalysis expects token-consumption companies to remove the 'seat' from software pricing, directly disrupting traditional SaaS incumbents including Salesforce, Workday, Adobe, SAP, ServiceNow, Atlassian and Microsoft.
insights.speaker: SemiAnalysis
insights.so_what: A pricing-model shift from seats to consumption attacks the per-seat revenue base of the entire enterprise software complex — a structural short thesis, not a cyclical one.
insights.quote: the rise of new token consumption companies removing the ‘seat’ from software sales
insights.locator: Track the disruption of traditional SAAS business models

insights.claim: The unit economics of the new SaaS model are framed as those of token consumers, with Cursor, Windsurf, Harvey and Perplexity cited as the archetypal token-consuming software companies whose cost of goods is inference.
insights.speaker: SemiAnalysis
insights.so_what: Software gross margins become a function of inference cost curves; falling cost-per-token is the margin lever that decides which AI app companies survive.
insights.quote: Token consumption software companies (Cursor, Windsurf, Harvey, Perplexity, etc)
insights.locator: Addressable market analysis of the token economy

insights.claim: SemiAnalysis separates AI compute demand sources (OpenAI, Anthropic, Thinking Machines, DeepSeek) from supply sources (CoreWeave, Nebius, Crusoe) and rates neocloud quality via its ClusterMAX ratings.
insights.speaker: SemiAnalysis
insights.so_what: Neocloud equities are not fungible — a quality rating on cluster delivery is the differentiator between contract wins and stranded capacity.
insights.quote: other quality neoclouds as measured by our ClusterMAX ratings
insights.locator: Detailed tracking of AI compute demand sources

insights.claim: SemiAnalysis splits AI-related revenue forecasting into three distinct streams — rental revenue, model revenue and software revenue — implying each layer of the stack should be valued on different margin and durability assumptions.
insights.speaker: SemiAnalysis
insights.so_what: Prevents double-counting AI revenue across the stack, and clarifies where the profit pool actually accrues versus where it is merely recycled.
insights.locator: AI-related revenue and profit forecast by business

insights.claim: Training demand is modeled as a function of model architecture development and expected ROIC, meaning SemiAnalysis treats future training buildouts as discretionary and return-gated rather than automatic.
insights.speaker: SemiAnalysis
insights.so_what: If expected ROIC on frontier training compresses, training orders can be cut quickly — the most volatile component of accelerator demand.
insights.quote: Training demand based on model architecture development and expected ROIC
